% SCI-PTC v0.1 shared normative equations -- owner-review candidate r0.5.
\section{Normative equations}
\label{sec:normative-equations}

The organizing detector-time model separates the latent correlated component
from its fitted estimate:
\begin{equation}
Y^{\rm CAL}_{td}=S_{td}+U_{\star,td}+N_{td},
\qquad
U_{\star,td}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}M_{\star,tk}A_{\star,dk}.
\label{eq:ptc-model}
\end{equation}
For the immutable fitted parent, distinguish the scaled-coordinate correlated
fit, its physical-unit realization, the operator-primary output, and the total
removed signal:
\begin{equation}
\widehat{\widetilde U}_{\rm corr}
  =\widehat M\widehat A^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
\widehat U_{\rm corr}=D\widehat{\widetilde U}_{\rm corr},
\qquad
Z=\mathcal A_{\Theta}(Y^{\rm CAL}),
\qquad
U_{{\rm total},\Theta}(Y^{\rm CAL})=Y^{\rm CAL}-Z.
\label{eq:ptc-subtraction}
\end{equation}
Equation~\ref{eq:ptc-subtraction} does not identify either removed quantity
with one physical contaminant. The exact application operator defines the
result; a fitted correlated component alone does not define how a new input
or response companion is acted on.

For declared learned additive location $\lambda$ and invertible internal
scaling $D$, the fitting coordinate and physical-unit application map are
\begin{equation}
Y'_c=C_{\lambda}(Y')=Y'-\lambda,
\qquad
\widetilde Y'=D^{-1}Y'_c,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\Theta}(Y')
=D\widetilde{\mathcal A}_{\Theta}(\widetilde Y').
\label{eq:center-scale}
\end{equation}
Scaling is restored for ordinary output; $\lambda$ is not. Detector $x$ has
no scientifically meaningful optical DC response, so the removed additive
reference is discarded and published in $\mathcal N_{\rm PTC}$. In
fixed-state application $\lambda$ is held fixed. In a full-procedure response
it is re-estimated in each run, may move under perturbation, and is again
discarded.

For the linear specialization
$\widetilde{\mathcal A}_{\Theta}(\widetilde Y')=L_{\Theta}\widetilde Y'$,
the correlated-subspace and total removed signals are
\[
U_{{\rm corr},\Theta}(Y')
=D(I-L_{\Theta})D^{-1}(Y'-\lambda),
\qquad
U_{{\rm total},\Theta}(Y')
=\lambda+U_{{\rm corr},\Theta}(Y').
\]

Facts and causes accumulate without erasure, while the exact named-use owner
supplies a complete required-restriction set evaluated under common T/F/U/C
knowledge semantics:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal C&=\bigcup_i\mathcal C_i,\\
\operatorname{Decision}_U&=
\begin{cases}
\texttt{ineligible},
  &\exists r\in\mathcal R_U:\ K(r)=\mathsf F,\\
\texttt{eligible},
  &\forall r\in\mathcal R_U:\ K(r)=\mathsf T,\\
\texttt{decision\_unavailable},
  &\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:cause-support}
\end{equation}
This rule follows exact request, structural binding, and applicability checks.
Known inapplicability yields no eligibility proposition. One applicable false
restriction cannot be rescued by another cause; all causes, unknowns, and
conflicts remain visible. PTC owns each PTC-use proposition, VAL evaluates the
supplied rule, and another named-use owner supplies its own proposition while
consuming the preserved facts.

An admitted group-local weighted or robust low-rank family minimizes
\begin{equation}
(\widehat M_g,\widehat A_g)=
\arg\min_{M,A}\sum_{t,d}w^{\rm fit}_{td}
\,\rho\!\left(\widetilde Y_{td}-(MA^{\mathsf T})_{td}\right),
\label{eq:masked-factor}
\end{equation}
where $w^{\rm fit}_{td}=0$ denotes no fit influence, not a zero-valued
observation. The loss, metric, support, rank, and missing-data semantics are
declared.

For a fixed supplied design $B$ and fit metric $\Omega$, a conditioned
regression family is
\begin{equation}
\widehat c=(B^{\mathsf T}\Omega B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\Omega y,
\qquad
\mathcal L_{B,\Omega}
=I-B(B^{\mathsf T}\Omega B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\Omega .
\label{eq:fixed-regression}
\end{equation}
The generalized inverse, tolerance, units, gauge, coefficient support, and
application support are material state.

A weighted common-mode family may estimate its temporal mode as
\begin{equation}
\widehat m_t=
\frac{\sum_d w^{\rm fit}_{td}\omega^{\rm cm}_{td}
      \widetilde Y_{td}}
     {\sum_d w^{\rm fit}_{td}\omega^{\rm cm}_{td}},
\label{eq:common-mode}
\end{equation}
only where the denominator is finite and nonzero. The aggregation weight
$\omega^{\rm cm}_{td}$, its unit, normalization, and population are declared;
it is not a fitted detector loading by implication.

For the ordinary configured-rank PCA/SVD route, application uses the frozen
group-local detector-loading subspace and mask-aware linear coefficient
recomputation. For centered row
$x_{g,t}=Y^{\rm CAL}_{g,t}-\lambda_g$,
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\widehat m^{\rm app}_{g,t}
&=x_{g,t}W^{\rm app}_{g,t}\widehat A_g
  \left(\widehat A_g^{\mathsf T}W^{\rm app}_{g,t}
  \widehat A_g\right)^+,\\
z_{g,t}
&=x_{g,t}-\widehat m^{\rm app}_{g,t}\widehat A_g^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:conditional-cleaner}
\end{equation}
The exact output support determines which entries of $z_{g,t}$ are published.
The generalized inverse, tolerance, detector binding, metric, support, and
insufficient-support state are frozen in $\Theta_g$. On complete uniform
support this reduces to detector-right projection through
$I-\widehat A_g(\widehat A_g^{\mathsf T}\widehat A_g)^+
\widehat A_g^{\mathsf T}$. Any temporal-left, two-sided,
detector/time-specific, or general vectorized family remains separately named
and is not inferred from matrix orientation or rank.

A separately named frozen-component subtraction family is
\begin{equation}
\widehat U_{\rm total}:=U_{{\rm total},\Theta}(Y^{\rm CAL}),
\qquad
\mathcal A^{\rm sub}_{\widehat U_{\rm total}}(Y')=Y'-\widehat U_{\rm total},
\qquad
D\mathcal A^{\rm sub}_{\widehat U_{\rm total}}[Y](H)=H.
\label{eq:frozen-component}
\end{equation}
It is not interchangeable with Equation~\ref{eq:conditional-cleaner} and is
not the base-v0.1 PCA/SVD application rule.

The ordinary route selects exactly one configured grouping level:
\begin{equation}
\mathcal G=
\begin{cases}
\{D_a\},&\text{array-level PCA},\\
\{D_{a,n}\}_n,&\text{network-level PCA}.
\end{cases}
\label{eq:hierarchy}
\end{equation}
Each $g\in\mathcal G$ has independent group-local support and resolved state.
The alternatives are not automatically sequential. A future hierarchical
family requires separate authority for its exact joint or sequential order.

For the ordinary route, the finite candidate-model set contains exactly the
explicitly requested positive-rank model specification:
\begin{equation}
\mathcal M_{{\rm cand},g}=\{c_g(k_{{\rm req},g})\},
\qquad
k_{{\rm req},g}\in\mathbb Z,
\qquad
1\le k_{{\rm req},g}\le k_{{\rm admissible},g}.
\label{eq:conjunctive-selection}
\end{equation}
The first route performs mathematical feasibility resolution, not automatic
scientific rank selection. Rank zero and unrealizable positive rank fail with
cause and no fallback, clipping, centering-only output, route conversion, or
map. A future automatic-selection family may use a separately authorized
conjunctive least-aggressive rule and must retain every predicate, threshold,
uncertainty treatment, order, tie, and rejected candidate in $\mathfrak L$.

The ordinary route performs one immutable-parent fit per configured group and
zero support-changing refinements. For a separately authorized future
refinement family, the immutable-parent lifecycle is
\begin{align}
\Theta_j&=\operatorname{Fit}(Y^{\rm CAL};\mathcal S_j),\nonumber\\
\mathcal S_{j+1}&=\operatorname{Classify}(Y^{\rm CAL},\Theta_j),\nonumber\\
\Theta_{j+1}&=\operatorname{Fit}(Y^{\rm CAL};\mathcal S_{j+1}).
\label{eq:immutable-refit}
\end{align}
Every fit uses the same immutable admitted CAL parent. A cleaned $Z_j$ is not
the next fit parent, and the final complete model is applied once.

The one-way state lifecycle is
\begin{equation}
R\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow O\longrightarrow
\mathfrak L\longrightarrow\Theta\longrightarrow\Lambda\longrightarrow\Pi ,
\label{eq:lifecycle}
\end{equation}
where learned evidence, resolved selection, numerical application, and
publication are distinct immutable states.

The full PTC procedure has separately typed signal and state projections:
\begin{equation}
\mathcal P(Y^{\rm CAL},R,E,O)
=\bigl(\mathcal P_Z(Y^{\rm CAL}),\mathcal P_{\Lambda}(Y^{\rm CAL})\bigr)
=(Z,\Lambda).
\label{eq:full-procedure}
\end{equation}

For fixed group-local resolved model $\Theta_g$, including frozen $\lambda_g$,
the local detector-time response and a realized CAL-grid companion are
\begin{equation}
J_{\Theta_g}[Y_g]=D\mathcal A_{\Theta_g}[Y_g],
\qquad
k_{{\rm src},g}^{\rm PTC\mid\Theta_g}
=J_{\Theta_g}[Y_g]\,k_{{\rm src},g}^{\rm CAL}.
\label{eq:local-companion}
\end{equation}
The companion uses the same group, support, mask, metric, rank, loading
subspace, generalized inverse, and tolerance as the data. The frozen
$\lambda_g$ is not subtracted from a perturbation and is not re-estimated.
If the parent is source-domain, the complete chain response is
\begin{equation}
k_{\rm src}^{\rm CAL}=K_{\rm up\to CAL}\tau_{\rm src},
\qquad
K_{\rm PTC\mid\Theta}=J_{\Theta}[Y]\circ K_{\rm up\to CAL},
\qquad
k_{\rm src}^{\rm PTC\mid\Theta}
=K_{\rm PTC\mid\Theta}\tau_{\rm src}.
\label{eq:conditional-response}
\end{equation}
Equations~\ref{eq:local-companion}--\ref{eq:conditional-response} are
alternative entry points for different companion parents;
$K_{\rm up\to CAL}$ is
never applied twice.

For a declared detector-time perturbation $h^{\rm CAL}$, the full-procedure
finite-perturbation signal response is
\begin{equation}
K_{\rm PTC}^{\rm proc}(\epsilon,h^{\rm CAL})=
\frac{\mathcal P_Z(Y^{\rm CAL}+\epsilon h^{\rm CAL})
      -\mathcal P_Z(Y^{\rm CAL})}{\epsilon}.
\label{eq:e2e-response}
\end{equation}
Each full-procedure evaluation re-estimates and again discards $\lambda$. The
corresponding state evidence, including any centering-state movement, is
retained separately:
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{\rm state}(\epsilon,h^{\rm CAL})=
\operatorname{Compare}_{\rm typed}\!\left[
\mathcal P_{\Lambda}(Y^{\rm CAL}+\epsilon h^{\rm CAL}),
\mathcal P_{\Lambda}(Y^{\rm CAL})\right].
\label{eq:e2e-state}
\end{equation}
Amplitude, side, source state, location, domain, and every changed rank, mask,
group, support, class, convergence, or fallback field are part of the result.

For response role $r\in\{\mathrm{fixed},\mathrm{procedure}\}$, the optional
map-center diagnostic is
\begin{equation}
\rho_{\rm center}^{\,r}
=e_{\rm center}^{\mathsf T}A_{\rm ref}k_{\rm src}^{\rm PTC,r}.
\label{eq:map-center}
\end{equation}
The exact response role, source-companion parent, reference MAP operator, and
center selector are mandatory factors. The diagnostic confers no MAP or
general beam authority.

For a fixed differentiable realized map, conditional covariance is
\begin{equation}
C_{Z\mid\Theta}=J_{\Theta}[Y]\,C_Y\,J_{\Theta}[Y]^{\mathsf T}.
\label{eq:conditional-covariance}
\end{equation}
For random selected state $\Theta$, the exact decomposition is
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Cov}(Z)=
\operatorname{E}\!\left[\operatorname{Cov}(Z\mid\Theta)\right]
+\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\operatorname{E}[Z\mid\Theta]\right).
\label{eq:total-covariance}
\end{equation}
Omitting the second term is a conditioned approximation, not complete
uncertainty.

A diagnostic indexed by detector or detector-time occurrence may take the
generic residual form
\begin{equation}
\eta_i=H_i(Z,\widehat U_{\rm corr},U_{{\rm total},\Theta},
\mathcal S,\Theta;\chi_H),
\label{eq:diagnostic}
\end{equation}
where $\chi_H$ records the domain, population/model reference, normalization,
support, uncertainty, and policy role.

A downstream analysis/gridding coefficient family is
\begin{equation}
\widetilde\gamma_i=f_{\gamma}(\eta_i;\chi_{\gamma}),
\qquad
\gamma_i=
\mathcal N_{\gamma}\!\left(
\widetilde\gamma_i;\{\widetilde\gamma_j:j\in\mathcal D_{\gamma}\}\right),
\label{eq:analysis-coefficient}
\end{equation}
where $i=d$ or $i=(t,d)$ is declared, $\mathcal D_{\gamma}$ is the exact
normalization domain, and $f_{\gamma}$ and $\mathcal N_{\gamma}$ are named
operators. The result is not precision unless separately proved.

Transitive causal influence for output $j$ is
\begin{equation}
\mathcal I_j=\bigcup_{i:\,i\rightarrow j}
\left(\{i\}\cup\mathcal I_i\right),
\label{eq:influence}
\end{equation}
including inputs that affect fitted state or selection even when a local
numeric derivative vanishes.

An explicit PTC-disabled request selects the RTC-terminal export route:
\begin{equation}
\mathsf{PTC\ request}=\mathsf{disabled}
\Longrightarrow
\mathsf{route}=\mathsf{RTC\_terminal\_export}
\Longrightarrow
\mathsf{terminal}=\mathsf{successful\ after\ complete\ RTC\ publication}.
\label{eq:disabled-route}
\end{equation}
CAL, PTC, and MAP are not entered and no products for those stages are
realized. Failure of the required RTC publication fails the route. Rank zero
is not an alias for this transition, and no direct CAL-to-MAP fallback exists
for ordinary Citlali reduction.
